findings.title: Neither toon ramp shows 3 bands: a white sphere spans only 13–25 luma, and from the game camera the lit side uses only the top of the ramp
findings.room: all rooms (measured in playground and lobby)
findings.problem: AGENTS 9 and DR-55 ask for a readable 3-step ramp. I measured it, and neither ramp gets close. I put a toon('#f4efe6') sphere (r 0.45 m) next to Pip at zoom 9 and sampled luma along its highest-contrast diameter. Default soft ramp: 13 luma range seen from the front (229→217), one plateau covering 93%. Seen from the side across the terminator: 25 range, 2 plateaus (65%/18%). ?hardcel: 18 range from the front, 1 plateau; 19 from the side, 2 plateaus (229/218, 46%/34%). ?hardcel&norim gives the same. Real props are just as flat. Crate faces measure top 172, front 155, side 152; the lobby cooler measures front 223, side 211, top 205 (soft) or 225/214 (hardcel). Three causes stack. (1) three.js samples the gradient at u = dotNL*0.5+0.5, so every surface facing the sun only reads the top half of the ramp. With the soft ramp (toon.ts:13: 92,96,120,168,196,226,246,255 with LinearFilter), that half is a smooth 196→255 gradient, not bands. With hardcel [90,185,255] it is 2 bands, and the dark band only appears where dotNL < −1/3. (2) The sun sits at (−11,21,13) (toon.ts:80), up and in front, on the camera's side, so the faces that would be in shadow point away from the camera at every default orbit. (3) Hemi 0.68–0.76 and ambient 0.12 (toon.ts:79, MOODS) lift the remaining shadow band, and ACES at exposure 1.02 crushes pale albedos into the shoulder. The comment at toon.ts:10-11 says the soft ramp gives 'three readable bands'. It does not: it is continuous shading. For the player, every pale prop reads as a flat cut-out with an outline and no form. Pip, the cooler, crates and white props merge with the pale floors (DR-54 asks props to sit ≥25 luma off the floor). The cel look the art direction promises never appears, with or without ?hardcel.
findings.fix: Make the ramp span the lit hemisphere and leave a visible terminator. (1) In toon() and glossyToon(), use onBeforeCompile to replace the toon gradient lookup (#include <lights_toon_pars_fragment> / getGradientIrradiance) with coord = vec2(clamp(dotNL,0.,1.), 0.). The whole ramp then maps to the faces the camera sees. (2) Make the default a real 3-band ramp: bands [105,185,255] with NearestFilter, or the soft variant [105,105,185,185,255,255] with LinearFilter so only the edges blend. Bands then switch near dotNL 0.33 and 0.66. (3) Drop hemi from about .7 to .45 and ambient from .12 to .06 (toon.ts:79 and the MOODS hemi values) so the shadow band is about 45–55% of lit. (4) Move the key light further to the side, e.g. sun.position (−18,21,2), so the terminator crosses the camera-facing half of props. (5) Fix the comment at toon.ts:10-11. Either way the product owner must sign off on one ramp (DR-55).
findings.verify: Re-run node mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/ramp2.mjs, then python mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/plateaus.py <shot>:<seedx>:<seedy>. Expect 3 plateaus each ≥15% of the diameter and ≥40 luma between the lit and shadow plateaus on the #f4efe6 sphere, at both the front and the side orbit. Also re-crop the playground crates: top, front and side faces should differ by ≥25 luma.
findings.verify_reason: The mechanism is confirmed in code. three r186 gradientmap_pars_fragment uses coord = dotNL*0.5+0.5 (node_modules/three/src/renderers/shaders/ShaderChunk/gradientmap_pars_fragment.glsl.js), so lit faces only sample texels 4–7 of the soft ramp (196,226,246,255) with LinearFilter (src/render/toon.ts:13-15), which is a continuous gradient rather than bands. With ?hardcel [90,185,255] and NearestFilter, the lit hemisphere gets 2 bands split at dotNL=1/3. I re-sampled toon-pipeline-05b myself. The sphere's horizontal diameter is 221–228 luma and its vertical diameter 209–229, so it is flat. In toon-pipeline-13, crate top/front are 166/152, a gap of only 14. The comment at toon.ts:10-11 ('three readable bands') is false. Priority goes down to P2: RULES.md DR-55 itself classes this as P2 needing a product-owner decision, and it doesn't block play or hurt teaching. The finding also misses that fill (0.45, from (16,9,8)) and rim (0.35, from (6,12,-18)) are extra DirectionalLights (toon.ts:84-85), each going through the same ramp with its own terminator. They fill in the sun's shadow side, which flattens the bands further. From other orbits the contrast is much higher: in toon-pipeline-06 I measured crate top 190, front 136, side 72. So 'at every default orbit' only holds for the start camera.

In the remap, mention that the fill/rim directional lights should either skip the ramp (add them as plain Lambert in RE_Direct, or lower them to about 0.2) or be removed in favour of hemi only. findings.title: The new rim light misses Pip, the cable and every coworker: glossyToon() overwrites it and toon().clone() silently drops it
findings.problem: The cool rim (toon.ts:20-31, WIP in 3631876) is meant to 'separate props from pale floors'. It is installed only through toon()'s onBeforeCompile and customProgramCacheKey 'toonRim' (toon.ts:39). Two paths lose it. (1) glossyToon() (actors.ts:9-18) builds its own MeshToonMaterial with a different onBeforeCompile and never calls rimShader. So Pip's helmet, mitts and boots (game.ts:155), the cable hose (actors.ts:78), the garage robot and the lamp shades get no rim. (2) Material.clone() does not copy onBeforeCompile or customProgramCacheKey; I confirmed in-page that toon(c).clone().onBeforeCompile !== toon(c).onBeforeCompile. Every cloned toon therefore renders without the rim. That covers all coworker blobs (shared vertex-colour clone, actors.ts:60 and kit.ts:95), occluder walls and pillars (decor.ts:47, :55), plain decor (decor.ts:19), confetti (particles.ts:17), every QFN part (qfn/station.ts:42), spectrum walls (spectrum/room.ts:21) and the lunch reset buttons (lunch-runtime.ts:60). Census of toon materials with no rim per level: lobby 9, playground 11, meeting 47 (28 of them blob white), lunch 52, arcade 20, garage 9, qfn 168, observatory 9, spectrum 16, plus 18–29 glossy meshes per level. The result is the opposite of DR-43: background clutter gets the separating edge, while the three shapes that must stand out most (Pip, the cable and the coworkers who react to chaos) don't. Next to each other, rimmed and unrimmed objects of the same colour also shade differently.
findings.fix: Export rimShader from toon.ts. In glossyToon (actors.ts:12), call rimShader(s) first, then apply the spec replace, which chains on the same '#include <opaque_fragment>' anchor (inject the rim before the spec mix), and make the cache key 'glossyToonRim'+spec+size. Add a helper in toon.ts, toonClone(m) => {const c=m.clone(); c.onBeforeCompile=m.onBeforeCompile; c.customProgramCacheKey=m.customProgramCacheKey; return c;}. Use it at actors.ts:60, kit.ts:95, decor.ts:19/47/55, particles.ts:17, qfn/station.ts:42, spectrum/room.ts:21 and lunch-runtime.ts:60. Big flat wall faces may stay rimless on purpose (DR-56 excludes them), but blobs, the cable and Pip must have it. Keep ?norim working.
findings.verify: Re-run node mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/materials.mjs. The 'toon(no rim/clone)' counts should drop to walls and plain decor only (no #ffffff blob entries, no QFN part colours), and glossy materials should report the rim cache key. Compare zoom-9 crops of Pip and a blob with and without ?norim: a cool edge should appear on Pip's helmet and the blob's top.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced in-page (mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap5-toon-pipeline/v1.mjs). toon(c).clone() has onBeforeCompile !== the original's, and its customProgramCacheKey falls back to the prototype default ('onBeforeCompile() {}') instead of 'toonRim'. Material.copy in three r186 (Material.js:1119-1199) copies userData but not onBeforeCompile. glossyToon's onBeforeCompile source contains no rim code (actors.ts:12-17). Scene census at playground start: 62 toon materials with the rim, 5 glossy without it, and 6 plain clones without it, including '#ffffff(vc)', the shared coworker blob material (actors.ts:60). Pip's hat/mitts/boots go through glossyToon (game.ts:155) and the cable through hoseMaterial→glossyToon (actors.ts:78). The core claim holds: the three most important shapes get no rim.

findings.title: Wedge and bridge are unbevelled knife-edge extrusions with no ink outline, and the wedge is the first job item in Lunch
findings.problem: The doorstop wedge (prefabs.ts, case 'wedge': ExtrudeGeometry with bevelEnabled:false) and the leak bridge (case 'bridge': same) are the only unbevelled prop bodies. My geometry audit flags both as UNBEVELLED (wedge 0.80×0.35×0.50, bridge 1.80×0.20×1.00). At zoom 9 the wedge reads as a flat yellow sheet ending in a razor tip. Its silhouette has almost no dark outline. Only the vertical back face and the rubber ribs are inked. The cause is that ExtrudeGeometry is non-indexed with flat per-face normals, so OutlineEffect's inverted hull splits at every hard edge and leaves gaps along the slope and tip. The wedge is the target of Lunch step 1 ('Wedge the kitchen door open…'), so the first item the player is asked to grab is the one with no outline and no form. It also breaks the 'chunky and soft' style. RESEARCH_ART R5.2 already prescribed the fix, but it was never built.
findings.fix: In both kindGeometry builders, use {depth:d-.04, bevelEnabled:true, bevelThickness:.02, bevelSize:.02, bevelSegments:2} and inset the shape by .02. Then call e=mergeVertices(e) (BufferGeometryUtils) followed by e.computeVertexNormals() so normals are smooth across the bevels and the outline hull stays closed. Round the wedge tip: start the shape at (−w/2, .025) instead of a zero-height point.
findings.verify: Re-run node mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/scale.mjs: no UNBEVELLED entries. Retake toon-pipeline-11/12 at zoom 9: the wedge should show a continuous ink silhouette and a lit chamfer on the slope edge.
findings.verify_reason: Both builders use ExtrudeGeometry with bevelEnabled:false. The cited line numbers are wrong: the bridge is at src/props/prefabs.ts:144 and the wedge at :178, not 136-137/163-167. The visual symptom is real. In toon-pipeline-11b and my own verify-gap5-toon-pipeline-01, the yellow wedge body has no dark silhouette ink on the slope, tip or sides; only the ribs (prefabs.ts:181) are outlined, and it blends into the yellow-brown Lunch wood floor. It is the Lunch step-1 item ('Wedge the kitchen door open with the doorstop'). The root cause (flat normals splitting the inverted hull) is plausible but I did not isolate it, because flat-normal boxes elsewhere still get outlines.
extra_evidence: src/props/prefabs.ts:144 (bridge), :178 (wedge): bevelEnabled:false

findings.fix_correction: Don't use mergeVertices + computeVertexNormals across the whole extrude. ExtrudeGeometry caps are triangulated only from outline vertices, so smoothed border normals would tilt the shading of the entire flat face. Instead, enable the bevel (bevelThickness/bevelSize .02–.03, bevelSegments 2–3) and run BufferGeometryUtils.toCreasedNormals(geo, Math.PI/4 or so). Bevel faces then shade smoothly while cap and slope faces stay flat. Also consider a darker wedge colour or a contrasting stripe, since #ffc94d on the Lunch wood floor is low contrast.

findings.title: Big rounded boxes are bevelled at 2.5–4.4% of their size (2 cm cap), so cabinets, vending, printers and crates read as sharp slabs
findings.problem: rbox() (kit.ts:17) caps the top and bottom edge bevel at Math.min(.02, h*.2, w*.15, d*.15), and box() (kit.ts:26) caps its radius at .025. DR-58 asks for ≥6% of the smallest dimension. Measured on the makeProp() models (bevel ÷ smallest dimension): printer 2.0 cm / 0.75 m = 2.7%, vending 2.5%, supply cart 2.5%, cabinet 3.0%, crate 3.3%, coffee machine 3.6%, cooler 3.9%, coolbox 4.2%, sofa 4.4%, capcart 5.6%. The vertical corners do get the r argument, but the horizontal top edges, which catch the light from the high camera, stay at 2 cm. At zoom 9 the crate and cabinet tops show a thin hard line rather than a lit chamfer. Because the extrude normals are flat (non-indexed), the 3-segment bevel also renders faceted. These are the largest, most repeated props (the Meeting has a wall of 1.6 m cabinets), so they set the style.
findings.fix: kit.ts:17: bevel=Math.min(Math.max(.015, Math.min(w,h,d)*.07), .06, h*.3, w*.2, d*.2). kit.ts:26: radius Math.min(.06, m*.1), with segments 3. Then mergeVertices and computeVertexNormals in rbox so the bevel shades smoothly. Templates are cached by key, so the draw-call cost stays the same.
findings.verify: Re-run node mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/scale.mjs: no extrude-bevel or rbox entry below 6% where the smallest dimension is > 0.25 m. Retake toon-pipeline-13 at zoom 9: crate and cabinet top edges should show a lit chamfer band of at least 3 px.
findings.verify_reason: kit.ts:17 caps the top/bottom bevel at Math.min(.02, h*.2, w*.15, d*.15). kit.ts:25 (box) caps the radius at Math.min(.025, m*.2). Crate: rbox(.7,.6,.7,.04), top bevel 2 cm = 3.3% of 0.6 m, below DR-58's 6%. RULES.md DR-58 already lists the 2.5 cm cap as a known fail on crates, so this isn't new, but it is unfixed. At zoom 9 (toon-pipeline-13) crate edges look slightly rounded, so 'thin hard line' overstates it a little.
extra_evidence: src/render/kit.ts:17 and :25 (box is line 25, not 26)
mockups/review5/RULES.md DR-58 'Check' (known fail on crates)
findings.fix_correction: The bevel formula change is fine. Don't do 'mergeVertices and computeVertexNormals in rbox'. The extrude caps have only outline vertices, so smoothed normals at the cap border would tilt the whole top-face shading. ExtrudeGeometry is also non-indexed with UVs that differ per face, so mergeVertices won't merge without deleting uv first. Use BufferGeometryUtils.toCreasedNormals(g, ~0.6 rad) instead, which smooths across bevel segments and keeps the caps flat.

findings.title: Gameplay parts are 2–4× real size, beyond DR-59's 1.2–1.5×: plug 0.42 m, strip 0.9 m, reel 0.67 m, splitter 0.62 m; chair seat +15%
findings.problem: I measured makeProp() bounding boxes (Box3, precise) against Pip, who measures 1.744 m in-game (feet 0.005 to helmet 1.749). That is within the 1.75–1.80 table, so Pip = 1.0. Results by kind (model size, then ratio to Pip, then verdict). Plug/coupler: 0.42 × 0.26 × 0.26 m, 0.24 Pip; a real plug body is about 0.08–0.10 m, so ×1.5 is ≤0.15. About 3× real and 180% over the rule; it is as thick as Pip's thigh. Power strip: 0.90 × 0.18 × 0.26 m, 0.52 Pip; a real 4-gang strip is 0.35–0.40 m, so ×1.5 is ≤0.60. 50–70% over. At the Meeting game camera it is about 70 px long next to a 120 px Pip. Cable reel: flange 0.672 m diameter, 0.39 Pip; a real 25 m reel is about 0.30 m, so ×1.5 is 0.45. 49% over. Splitter: 0.62 × 0.275 × 0.40 m; a real one is 0.10–0.15 m, so 4× over. Chair: seat top 0.57–0.59 m against the table's 0.5, 14–18% over. These are within ±10%: mug 0.18 × 0.20 (equal to the table's 0.16 × 0.2, about 10 px at the game camera, so above the 8 px floor), desk top 0.95 ✓, monitor 0.63 × 0.48 ✓, beanbag 0.90 × 0.61 with seat dent at 0.37 ✓, crate 0.70 × 0.61 ✓, cabinet 1.60 ✓, cooler 1.25 ✓, lobby door leaf 2.26 (+3%) ✓. The standing blob is 1.01 m: −8% from 1.1 and just under the 1.05 lower bound. The table also contradicts itself: R6.2 sets the mug at 0.2 m, which is 2.1× a real 9.5 cm mug, against its own '1.2–1.5×'. The oversized job parts make Pip look like a toddler next to his tools. The strip at half Pip's height and the reel at knee height undercut 'one scale' and make desks look small.

findings.title: Models overhang their physics boxes by up to 19 cm, so props can sit inside each other at rest and g.audit can't see it
findings.problem: prefabs.ts:9 says 'models below are drawn to fit inside it (the physics box)'. Measured, many don't (model w×h×d against collider size). Plug/coupler 0.42 vs 0.30 long: the pins stick 12 cm out of the collider, which is why the plug's prongs poke through the socket box. Splitter 0.62 vs 0.50 (inlet and outlet stubs). Mail cart 1.34 vs 1.20 wide and 0.945 vs 0.65 tall (the push bar). Coolbox 1.10 × 0.79 vs 1.00 × 0.60: the handle and lid rise 19 cm above the collider top. Supply cart 1.84 vs 1.70. Capcart 1.74 vs 1.60. Dolly 1.34 vs 1.20. Plant 0.70 vs 0.58 (leaves). Whiteboard depth 0.50 vs 0.20 (feet). Printer depth 0.92 vs 0.75. Desk height 1.15 vs 0.95 (clutter on top, which is acceptable). The cooler is the reverse: model 0.51 vs collider 0.60, so it stands 4.5 cm clear of anything touching it. Rapier collides the boxes, not the meshes, so at rest and after throws the overhangs interpenetrate other props and walls. For example, a prop stacked on a coolbox sinks into its handle, and carts parked side by side merge their bars. g.audit(0.02) works from colliders, so it reports these as clean (DR-70).
findings.fix: Make the collider match the visual. Either (a) grow the prefab sizes to the measured model bounds where the overhang is solid body (coolbox h .79, cart [1.34,.95,.75], supply [1.84,…], capcart [1.74,…], dolly [1.34,…]), or (b) keep the box and add small compound colliders for the bars and pins in addProp (game.ts:124). Shrink the cooler collider to [.52,1.25,.52]. Add a unit test that asserts Box3(makeProp(k)) ⊆ prefab size + 2 cm for every kind except a whitelist (desk clutter, plant leaves).
findings.verify: Unit test over Object.keys(prefabs) comparing Box3.setFromObject(makeProp(k),true) with prefabs[k].size (reuse mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/scale.mjs logic), and g.audit(.02) at start on every level.

findings.title: Gloss is used on painted wood (the nine 3.7 m² lobby door leaves) and on metals the rule doesn't list
findings.problem: The material census of all 10 levels finds no MeshStandard, Phong, Lambert or Physical materials, and no glossy fabric or paper. That part of DR-57 passes. The breaks: all 9 lobby door leaves use glossyToon('#fffaf0',{spec:.5,size:.97}) on a 1.66 × 2.26 m rounded slab (hub/lobby.ts:90). They are painted wood doors, the largest glossy surfaces in the game, and the colour is the same #fffaf0 as paper sheets, so they look like lacquered paper. Gloss also lands on metal and appliance parts outside the 'hard plastics only' list: the garage tool chest (steel, garage/room.ts:93); the spectrum copper fence posts and rails, merged into one 4 × 2.2 × 6.6 m glossy mesh (spectrum/room.ts:102-103); the observatory telescope tube (observatory/room.ts:77); the spectrum toaster (room.ts:112); the copper coil tori (observatory/station.ts:41); and the garage motor (garage/station.ts:134). The specular in glossyToon also uses a light direction fixed in view space (actors.ts:14, L=(−.35,.75,.55) against vViewPosition), so the highlight stays on the same screen side whatever the sun does. Seen from behind (toon-pipeline-12) Pip's helmet shows a highlight on its back while his shadow falls toward the camera.
findings.fix: hub/lobby.ts:90: replace the glossyToon with toon('#fffaf0'), or a wood-door colour such as '#f3e6cf' so it no longer matches paper. findings.title: Round parts built outside the kit skip the ≥24-segment rule (lamp shades 14–20, tori 6, accessories 6–16)
findings.problem: kit.ts doubles segments to at least 24 for cyl() and sphere(), but about 40 direct new T.*Geometry calls bypass it. Lamp shades: CylinderGeometry 20 (decor.ts:90, dressing.ts:53, lunch-runtime.ts:111) and 18 (decor.ts:164). Desk-lamp cones: 14 (prefabs.ts:49, dressing.ts:65). Garage work-lamp cone: 16 (garage/room.ts:106). Tori with a radial segment count of 6: the mop bucket bail and the coolbox handle (prefabs.ts mop/coolbox). Coworker accessories: 6–16 (actors.ts:36-51, e.g. the antenna cylinder at 6). The spectrum beam cylinder: 10 (spectrum/station.ts:272). The objective marker cone: 20 (objectives.ts:98). Under the ink outline these show as visible polygon steps at zoom 9. The open-ended shades are the worst, since their rims are outlined edge-on.
findings.fix: Add cone() and torus() helpers to kit.ts that apply the same Math.max(24, seg*2) rule (tubular segments ≥ 32, radial ≥ 10), and switch the direct calls above to cyl(), cone(), torus() or sphere(). Open shades can pass openEnded through a cyl() option.

findings.fix_correction: Apply the ≥24 rule based on on-screen size, not to every primitive. Raise shades, cones and decor.ts:156 to ≥32 segments. Leave sub-2 cm details (eye glints, thin torus tubes) whitelisted, since doubling their segments inside the merged blob geometry only adds vertices with no visible gain. notes.models: Material census, from a scene traverse in every level through a patched Object3D.onBeforeRender: every lit surface is MeshToonMaterial. The rest are MeshBasicMaterial for screens, decals and unlit floor marks, ShaderMaterial only for the lobby portals, and sprites for glow. There are zero MeshStandard, Phong, Lambert or Physical materials, and the GLB Pip is fully converted to toon. No glossy fabric or paper exists, and the only glossy wood is the lobby door leaves. Gloss otherwise covers the intended plastics: Pip's helmet, mitts and boots (#fdd161, #f6f2e5, #424b65), the cable hose, the fridge, the bots and the lamp shades, plus several metals that need a product-owner ruling. The real pipeline gaps are the ramp (the visible shading range on pale props is tiny) and the rim being lost on glosses and clones. Scale: Pip is 1.744 m, the blob 1.01 m, the desk top 0.95, the cabinet 1.6 and the door 2.26. The handheld and job parts are where scale breaks (2–4× real). Bevels: RoundedBoxGeometry parts are fine for small pieces, but big rbox bodies cap at a 2 cm bevel, and the wedge and bridge are unbevelled with no outline.
notes.clarity: The flat ramp hurts readability most on pale props over pale floors. With 13–25 luma of form shading, separation comes only from the outline and the new rim, and the rim is missing on Pip, coworkers and the cable. The wedge, Lunch's first job item, has no outline on its slope.
notes.fun: Not directly in scope. The oversized plug, reel and strip make the cable kit look toy-like, which suits the comedy, but it should be a declared multiplier rather than ad hoc sizes.
notes.playability: No errors: g.close() returned [] for every run (10 levels in materials.mjs, plus the ramp, scale, pip and bevel scripts). Collider-versus-model overhangs (up to 19 cm on the coolbox) are a latent overlap issue that the audit can't see.
